questions.prompt: When should the island count increase during the grid scan?

choices.label: Whenever any land cell is encountered, even if visited.
choices.feedback: One search covers a complete connected island, so only the start of that search adds one island.

choices.label: When an unvisited land cell starts a new flood search.
choices.feedback: One search covers a complete connected island, so only the start of that search adds one island.

choices.label: Whenever a land cell touches water.
choices.feedback: One search covers a complete connected island, so only the start of that search adds one island.

questions.prompt: When should a cell be marked visited?

choices.label: Only after the entire grid scan is complete.
choices.feedback: Marking on entry prevents neighboring cells from repeatedly recursing back into each other.

choices.label: Before recursively exploring its land neighbors.
choices.feedback: Marking on entry prevents neighboring cells from repeatedly recursing back into each other.

choices.label: Only after all its neighbors have finished searching.
choices.feedback: Marking on entry prevents neighboring cells from repeatedly recursing back into each other.

questions.prompt: Which cells should that flood search visit next?

choices.label: Only land cells diagonal to the current cell.
choices.feedback: An island is connected through horizontal and vertical land neighbors.

choices.label: Every land cell anywhere in the grid.
